clue.text: Novelist needing to raise capital

parts.note: to jack, as in jack up a car, is to raise
London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: A struggling writer needs to find investment money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' reads as money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author of The Call of the Wild is a famous novelist.

clue.text: Beetle found on top of each fibrous plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it comes before it

parts.note: to beetle is to overhang or project, as beetling brows do, so it means jut

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down answer is its first letter

explanation.surface: An insect turns up perched on each plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like the insect, but here it is the verb meaning to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: Jute is a plant grown for the coarse fibre used in sacking and hessian.

clue.text: Order to desist, so visit cancelled

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A visit is cancelled after an order to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off dogs or an attack is to order them to stop.

clue.text: You've not to mention about spring — it's OK as it is

indicators.note: one phrase goes about, that is around, the other

parts.note: let alone, as in 'I can't walk, let alone run', means not to mention
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet about a spring because things are fine as they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' but is the container signal; 'You've' only introduces the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To let well alone is to leave something unchanged because it is fine already.

clue.text: New weapon, limited in scope

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon fired from a bow

explanation.surface: A new weapon has only a limited range.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow is a synonym for restricted, having little breadth or range.

clue.text: Make repairs above lobby, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard spoken, so these words are a sound-alike

parts.note: over means above and a hall is a lobby

explanation.surface: Builders do repairs to the floor above the entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to examine it thoroughly and repair it.

clue.text: Transfer to be approved

definitions.meaning: to hand it on, as in football
an exam candidate or a bill that ... is approved

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday uses of the same verb: handing over, and getting through a test.

clue.text: Article on Dynasty captivating America might be funny

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: something captivating holds another piece inside it

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: An article about the TV soap Dynasty that delights Americans could be comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynasty' looks like the 1980s American TV soap, but it is a Chinese imperial dynasty; 'captivating' signals holding one piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing is a direct synonym for funny or entertaining.

clue.text: Conservative, after drinks, makes up a tale

indicators.note: the party member comes after the drinks

parts.note: shorts are small measures of spirits
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician, having had a few drinks, invents a story.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORTS are small drinks of spirits, as opposed to long drinks like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short story is a tale brief enough to read in one sitting.

clue.text: Don't mince words in republic following speech

indicators.note: the republic comes after the speech

parts.note: talk means speech
Turkey is a republic

explanation.surface: A politician speaks frankly when giving a speech about a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is an idiom for speaking plainly and getting down to business.

clue.text: Embrace old writer

parts.note: a hug is an embrace

explanation.surface: Someone hugs an elderly author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' seems to describe the writer, but it supplies O.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo, author of Les Miserables, was a French writer.

clue.text: Rise in recognition

definitions.meaning: an increase in value, as in property values going up

explanation.definitionFit: Appreciation means both an increase in value and the recognition of merit.

clue.text: Reach small promontory and stop rambling?

definitions.meaning: to arrive at a headland, a point being a small promontory
to get to the main issue instead of talking around it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means getting to the essential matter; read literally it is arriving at a headland.

clue.text: Bug flotilla's leader on run out on grand barge

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
G is short for grand, a thousand
a hopper is a barge that carries dredged mud or spoil

explanation.surface: The leading vessel of a small fleet runs aground out on a big barge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. RO is how a cricket scorecard records a batsman run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A froghopper is a small jumping insect, a true bug whose larvae make cuckoo spit.

clue.text: Upset the composure of two females entering government

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: rule means government
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them make FF

explanation.surface: Two women join the government and upset the ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle someone is to disturb their calm, as wind ruffles feathers.

clue.text: Dismissed just claim completely

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a right is a just claim or entitlement

explanation.surface: A fair claim is thrown out entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely or wholly, as in winning outright.

clue.text: Home of little value used jointly

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
common things are ordinary, cheap and plentiful

explanation.surface: A cheap house is shared by several people.
explanation.definitionFit: Things held in common are owned or used by people jointly.

clue.text: Butterfly angrily struggling against force of gravity

indicators.note: the letters of angrily struggle into a new order

parts.note: g is the symbol for the acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A butterfly flaps angrily, fighting to rise against gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily struggling' paints a fluttering insect, but 'struggling' is the anagram signal; 'against' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a brown European butterfly (and also a fish).

clue.text: Finally full of energy, if nothing else

indicators.note: one piece contains the other

parts.note: at last means finally
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone finally bursts with energy, if nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: At least means at any rate, as in 'at least he tried', if nothing else.

clue.text: Cake Alice baked —- last piece for Hatter

indicators.note: baking turns ingredients into something new, so the letters are mixed
the last piece of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Alice, at the Mad Hatter's tea party, saves the final slice of cake for the Hatter.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry cake filled with cream.

clue.text: Football club magazine

definitions.meaning: a famous north London football club
a store for weapons and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a weapons store, and Arsenal is the London football club named after one.

clue.text: Publishers' head very annoyed one infringing copyright

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter

parts.note: irate means very angry

explanation.surface: The head of a publishing house is furious at someone breaking copyright.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who copies books or music illegally is called a pirate.

clue.text: One girl entering party behind Rosalind's lover, a composer

indicators.note: the party comes after the lover

parts.note: Orlando loves Rosalind in Shakespeare's As You Like It

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the Roman numeral one
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl crashes a party with Rosalind's beau, a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando di Lasso was a Renaissance Flemish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando di Lasso, also called Lassus, was a leading 16th-century composer.

clue.text: Refuse in study, and close to study

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go into the study and stays close to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a request is to refuse it.

clue.text: Drawing of flat, incomplete

indicators.note: the word is left without its final letter

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface

explanation.surface: The sketch of an apartment is unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means a level PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scale drawing, especially of a building seen from above.

clue.text: Intolerance shown by G&S character after I married

indicators.note: the character comes after the other pieces

parts.note: Patience is the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera

explanation.surface: Someone loses patience with a Gilbert and Sullivan role after marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S are Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of comic operas including Patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is an unwillingness to put up with delay or with others, an intolerance.

clue.text: Legal documents, reportedly for Swiss hotelier

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so this is a sound-alike

parts.note: writs are formal legal documents

explanation.surface: Legal papers are served on a Swiss hotel owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cesar Ritz was the Swiss founder of the famous luxury hotels.

clue.text: Popular high flier meeting supporter within

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a tern is a seabird, a flier
an ally supports you

explanation.surface: A well-liked high-achiever meets a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high flier' suggests a successful person, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Internally means on the inside, so it can stand for within.
